variants.headline: Builder left unpaid for work done
variants.sub: The builder {builder} is owed payment by the client {client} for completed work.
variants.body:
The client {client} has not paid the builder {builder} for work done. The amount owed is {owed}. After three missed months the builder stops work. For {target}, the event raises the basic question of responsibility when a construction undertaking requires payment as well as performance.

The work was done. The payment has not been made. It is a plain story about an obligation, without needing a fictional argument at the site. Remember the difference between a missed payment and the later stopping rule before somebody turns the account into a stoppage that has not been established.

We criticise {target} on the standard of contractual responsibility. Work done should not be treated as though payment were optional, and a missed obligation deserves more than a convenient explanation of why scrutiny should wait. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
